answer: An agent market requires every identity, whether prism, beacon, or raven, to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for work, and caps each identity at one active job. Creating extra keys is free, but activating 1,000 fake agents ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes parallel access costly, so an attacker must finance real locked capital to multiply its presence.
